definition: A decoding strategy that samples multiple chain-of-thought reasoning paths for the same question and selects the most consistent final answer among them.
details: Self-consistency improves reasoning accuracy by treating agreement across diverse reasoning paths as a signal of correctness, rather than relying on a single greedy generation.

explainer.lead: Self-consistency samples several chain-of-thought reasoning paths for one question and picks the most consistent final answer. It matters because agreement across diverse paths signals correctness better than a single greedy generation.

tiers.eli5: Ask the same question several times and go with the answer most attempts agree on, instead of trusting just the first try.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to raise reasoning accuracy by sampling multiple reasoning paths and taking the most consistent final answer. The cost is that multiple samples multiply compute versus one greedy generation.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is a decoding strategy: sample multiple chain-of-thought paths for the same question and select the most consistent final answer among them. It relies on agreement across paths as a correctness signal rather than a single greedy generation.

explainer.example: For a math word problem, the model samples five reasoning paths; three end in 42 and two in other values, so 42 is selected.

citation.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
